title.narrative: Racism and Social Inequalities in Mental Health in Brazil (ORI)

description.narrative:
Brazil is a highly unequal society. Systemic racism is experienced daily by Black Brazilians, who commonly live in socioeconomically deprived areas, with poor infrastructure and lack of access to healthcare. This leads to sharp health inequalities, with a major effect on mental health outcomes. To date, no focused research or specific interventions and health policies address these inequalities in mental health outcomes between Black and White Brazilians.
There is an urgent need to study this through an intersectional approach. Mental health can be affected by several aspects of one’s identity, including race, gender, age, employment, socioeconomic status and place of residence. Intersectional research means considering all such intersecting identity markers and explaining how this intersection causes greater inequalities for certain groups.
ORI is a 4-year global health research programme with the strategic aim to improve mental health outcomes of Black underserved Brazilians, through co-producing interventions with community members, mental healthcare professionals and policy stakeholders. The ORI team brings together uniquely combined, international expertise and is diverse in terms of gender, race, clinical and academic backgrounds and academic career level.
ORI has six objectives:
To co-produce intersectional knowledge about the effects of racism and social disadvantage on mental health in Brazil
To co-develop, based on the new evidence mental health awareness campaigns for communities and training packages for professionals working in health, education and social sectors
To influence mental health policy at municipal, state and national levels in Brazil
To share findings and best practice with stakeholders in the Latin American and Caribbean region
To train researchers from anthropology, psychiatry, psychology, public health, and epidemiology to become future mental health research leaders
To conduct socially engaged research and co-produce knowledge with Black Brazilians
In every aspect of ORI, we will engage and involve community members in a context-appropriate and culturally bespoke way and always connect scientific knowledge with local cultural knowledge.
A particular strength of ORI lies in the collaboration with 12 project partners from the health community, civil society, government and the international science community. The ORI dissemination strategy will achieve maximum social and academic impact to improve health outcomes.
